_: ROADMAP K45(b3) — what the timber's detail control does, banked. Read by tools/measure_timber_detail.mjs --gate, measured on the PUBLISHED mirror at 1280x800. The woody layer is planted over the whole field once rather than into a ring that follows the visitor, so unlike the sward its population does not depend on the viewport.
measured_against: the published mirror, walked through window.__chicago4d.setDetail

before._: the same three levels before K45(b3), on the same mirror. The tree counts are the measurement that says the control was inert: 472/470/437 is one wood planted three times, and what moved was the point-bar screen, which is the one population that must not move.

tolerance._: A Bernoulli acceptance over ~190,000 cells: the tree count is near-Poisson, so 0.06 of full's 472 trees is about 1.8 sigma. It carries a second error as well, and this is why the figure is not tighter — the sampling step moves the count on its own. Before any keep fraction existed the three levels planted 472/470/437, so light's grid alone reads 7 % below full's, and light's measured share here is 0.544 against a nominal 0.60. band_share is the northernmost tenth of the swept field's share of the stems — full's is 19.2 %, and a truncated wood empties it outright.

reach._: The swept field runs to N +397.7 m at full. A stem budget bound partway through a south-to-north loop pulls this down and is the failure mode K45(b2) found at light's old cap of 300.

screen._: The sandbar-willow point bar. It does not take the keep fraction — a screen needs its clumps to touch — and since K45(b3) it does not thin with the sampling step either. The floor is under 1 because a 6-9 m bar sampled on a 5.6 m grid has fewer points than the screen wants stools, and the roll saturates at 1 rather than exceeding it.
